summary: Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of Winnipeg, University of Calgary, and McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen, she held posts at St. Paul's University College (attested 2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

Max Deeg works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. After earning his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg, he served as Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021).

Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University (1889–1891). He held positions at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, and Dropsie College (1909–1932).
Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch, finishing in 1913.

Max Oidtmann specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Tibetology, having studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott. He held posts at Georgetown University in Qatar (2013–2021), Georgetown University (~2014–2020), and the University of Munich (~2020).

Philosopher Max Scheler studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. Over his career, he held academic posts at Jena (~1900–1906), Munich (~1907–1910), Göttingen, and Cologne (~1919–1928).
Max Uhle was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Leipzig University (~1876–1880) under Georg von der Gabelentz.

Max Walleser, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nürnberg. He founded the Institut für Mahāyāna-Buddhismus and taught at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936).
Max von Waldberg studied at Chernivtsi University (~1877–1881) and later held an academic post at Heidelberg University (~1889–1933).

Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and University of Paris (~1957–1979).
May Oung studied at the University of Cambridge (~1904–1907) and worked in history and archaeology. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.
Historian Maya Jasanoff studied at Harvard College, the University of Cambridge, and Yale University. She held posts at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) and Harvard University (~2009).
McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and the University of Chicago under Clyde Kluckhohn. He served as professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago (~1955–1998).

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and Nanjing University. He held posts at the University of Colombo (~2005) and as visiting lecturer at other institutions.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Meei-Hwa Chern works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under John Raines (attested 2000) and served as a visiting researcher at Academia Sinica.
Megan Bryson, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells, later serving as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).
Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology, having completed a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and teacher Dieter Schuh.
